This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- for the death of Sri. SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2978/2023 Manjunath S/o Late Venkategowdaiah in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 04.04.2023 at about 8.45 a.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Manjunath was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-K-6376 and when he reached near Rajaghatta Lake, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, at that time,
one Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B-6066 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed so as to endanger to human life and came on extreme right side and dashed to the Petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the impact, Manjunath had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body and died on the spot.
Thereafter, Post mortem was conducted at Government hospital, Doddaballapura and body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2978/2023
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Sericulturist and was earning a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Manjunath, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B-6066.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Rathnamma vs Nanjundeshwara.

3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statements to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Manjunath SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2978/2023 in the said accident.
Further he contended that the alleged accident occurred mainly on the negligence of the deceased, not due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further he contended that the driver had valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
Further he contended that offending vehicle was duly insured with the Respondent No.2.
Hence, he is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Manjunath in the said accident.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the same and the vehicle was not having valid Permit and Fitness Certificate to ply on the road as on the date SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2978/2023 of alleged accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Manjunath S/o Late Venkategowdaiah was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred 04.04.2023 at about 8.45 a.m., on Rajaghatta - Doddaballapur road, near Rajaghatta Lake, Kasaba Hobli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B-6066?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Manjunath?
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2978/2023 3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If yes,
what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

4) What Order or Award ?

3 5.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 22 documents at Ex.P.1 to 22 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.1 and 2 did not choose to lead evidence.

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions,
documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2978/2023  REASONS
7. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that Manjunath was died in the accident that occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B-6066 by its driver.
8. On the other hand, the Respondents had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper lorry by its driver.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P22.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint lodged by one Shantharaju S/o Late Baiyanna, the Doddaballapura Rural Police have registered the case against the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B- SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2978/2023 6066 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.5 is the Inquest mahazar.
Ex.P6 is the PM report which shows the cause of death is due to severe Haemorrage & shock due to the multiple grievous injuries to the chest, head and the right forearm due to Road Traffic Accident.

Ex.P-7 is the true copy of the Charge- Sheet which shows that the Doddaballapura Rural Police have submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Tipper lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
12.

The Charge-Sheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending Tipper lorry for rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and causing the accident and due to the said accident, the husband of the PW-1 had succumbed to the injuries.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondents did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondents have failed to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper lorry and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."
 SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2978/2023  13. Issue No.2 and 3:
Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
14. The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and Petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Manjunath.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of deceased and Petitioners at Ex.P.13 to 17.
Hence, the said documents shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Manjunath, they entitled for the compensation.
15. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 52 years and deceased was working as a Sericulturist and was earning Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
PW.1 has produced 8 RTCS which shows the said properties stands in the name of the deceased Manjunath.

But, the Petitioners have not produced the documents to show the income derived from the Sericulture SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2978/2023 and they have not produced the Bank Statement of the deceased Manjunath.
It is also worth to note here that on the death of deceased Manjunath, the Petitioners can continue the Agriculture and Sericulture in the said properties.
Therefore, it is proper to take the notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Manjunath as 52 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.13 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Manjunath which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1971.
The alleged accident was occurred on 04.04.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Manjunath was 52 years, 3 months and 3 days.

Hence,
the age of the deceased Manjunath to be taken at 53 years for the purpose of assessment.

With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2978/2023 sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind him his wife, children and mother.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife,
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and the Petitioner No.4 is the mother and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2978/2023 rate of 10%
in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.

Further,
the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are the wife, children and mother of the deceased Manjunath, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
20.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and they lost their father's love and car and the Petitioner No.4 is the mother of deceased Manjunath, who lost SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2978/2023 son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
21.
The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
22.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.16,000/- pm.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2978/2023 At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.

wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40 Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2978/2023 computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork: executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 10% when the age is between 50 to 60 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 53 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 10% of the income has to be added.

So, 10% of Rs.
16,000/- comes to Rs.1,600/-.
Therefore, the income of the SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2978/2023 deceased comes to Rs.17,600/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + Rs.1,600/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2978/2023  2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-

 dead body  6. Loss of Dependency Rs.17,42,400/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.20,27,300/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

26. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-B-6066.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2978/2023 Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,27,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,27,300/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the SCCH 15 21 Rathnamma vs Nanjundeshwara.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39417641/

The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1.
3) 10% to the Petitioner No.4.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3, 50% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 respectively by way of SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2978/2023 E-payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.4 is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.4 by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.
 The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.

The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are apportioned among them are as shown below:

3) 10% to the Petitioner No.4.

The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.4 is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.4 by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.
 The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
 Draw Award accordingly.
